_meta.description: Position-specific priority attributes — what scouts at a Pro Academy level look for at each age bracket. Each priority_attribute carries a weight (1-5, used to order the reference card by importance) and a 'why_matters' line explaining the scout's lens. The reference range ('pro_academy_range') is the typical score band a player needs to show in the AI's existing benchmarks to sit at Pro Academy level. We don't claim UEFA endorsement; this is a curated framework aligned with the same youth-development pillars used across European Category-1 academies.

priority_attributes.why_matters: Top CBs win 80% of their work through position before duels happen.
When to step, when to drop, when to pass — separates pro from amateur CBs.
Aggressive 1v1 defending in big moments defines the role.
Reading runners off the ball and adjusting position early.
Modern CBs build out from the back — both feet under pressure.
Aerial duels and shielding the ball through contact.
Voice and presence to organise the back line.
Modern FBs need explosive 5m starts to attack and recover.
1v1 defending against wingers is the position's signature test.
Up and down the flank for 90 minutes — endurance is non-negotiable.
Final-third delivery quality (cross, cut-back, switch) creates chances.
Defensive shape — when to tuck in vs stay wide.
Overlapping/underlapping at the right moment without leaving the line exposed.
Tireless tracking back after attacking — the role demands it.
Screening the back four is positional first, athletic second.
Reads the danger before it materialises — head on a swivel.
Controls tempo with accurate simple passes under pressure.
When to step into a duel vs hold position — pure game IQ.
Wins midfield battles — sets the tone for the team.
90-minute engine to cover the middle channel.
Top CMs scan 2-3 times per possession — this is the #1 separator at academy level.
Risk vs security with the ball — the pro-level CM judges this perfectly.
Range and line-breaking quality is the heartbeat of the role.
Receiving in tight central spaces requires elite touch.
Pro academy CMs sustain press-intensity across 90 minutes.
Both-footed CMs can receive on either side — pros expect at least 5/10.
Brave in central duels even against bigger physical opponents.
AMs make 50+ decisions per match in the most congested area of the pitch.
Top AMs see the picture before receiving — pockets between lines are the key habit.
Final pass quality (weight, disguise, timing) separates AMs at every level.
Receiving in tight spaces under pressure — non-negotiable for the role.
Finding pockets and timing arrivals is half the AM's job.
Beating one defender unlocks the next phase of attack.
End product from the edge of the box — quality strike is expected at Pro Academy level.
Wingers win primarily through first-step explosiveness.
1v1 beats unlock the cross/shot — the defining skill of the role.
Isolating and beating the full-back is the winger's central test.
Top-end speed to threaten in behind on diagonal balls.
Final ball quality (cross / cut-back / cutback) defines chance creation.
Inverted wingers especially need to finish from the half-space.
Switchable wingers (play either flank) need both feet.
Pro academy strikers finish chances — the most prized attribute at every level.
Creating separation in the box is half the goal-scoring battle.
Late, perfectly-timed runs beat the offside line and find space.
Receiving under pressure with one touch to set up the shot.
Holding the ball up with back to goal — every #9 needs this.
Beating the last line and creating goal-side separation.
Brave in the box — strikers get fouled and have to play through it.
Saving 1v1s is the GK's signature high-leverage moment.
Starting position determines half of all save outcomes.
Reactive saves require explosive change of direction.
When to claim, when to stay, when to come for the cross.
Modern GKs build attacks — short and long distribution accuracy.
Voice and presence — the back four reads the keeper's energy.
Reading the play to start position correctly before the ball arrives.
